A first stop before [Classic Drum Machines Compared](drum-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the MPC60 is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **MPC60** was made by **Akai**, designed by **Roger Linn**, and released on **8 December 1988** (Wikipedia, "Akai MPC").
- It is a **sampler**: you record any sound into it, then play it from **16 pads** (MPC60 manual, pp. 15, 18).
- Wikipedia: its affordability "had a democratizing effect": people could make tracks without a studio.

## Its sound

- Samples are **12-bit at 40 kHz**, which gives a gritty sound (MPC60 manual, p. 15).
- The pads feel how hard you hit: **velocity** (manual, p. 5).
- **Swing** goes from 50 % (straight) to 75 %; 66 % is a triplet, and the manual suggests 54 % or 62 % (manual, p. 44).
- **Timing correct** moves notes onto the grid; turned off, the notes stay where you played them (manual, p. 43).

## Guided tour

Each step plays two bars. Letters in the hi-hat row are softer (a) to harder (z) hits.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-pat="{&quot;bpm&quot;:92,&quot;rows&quot;:{&quot;kick&quot;:&quot;x......x..x.....&quot;,&quot;snare&quot;:&quot;....x.......x...&quot;,&quot;chh&quot;:&quot;x.x.x.x.x.x.x.x.&quot;}}"><p><b>On the grid.</b> Timing correct 1/16, swing 50 %. Listen: straight and tidy.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-pat="{&quot;bpm&quot;:92,&quot;rows&quot;:{&quot;kick&quot;:&quot;x......x..x.....&quot;,&quot;snare&quot;:&quot;....x.......x...&quot;,&quot;chh&quot;:&quot;t.h.t.h.t.h.t.h.&quot;}}"><p><b>Velocity.</b> Hard and soft hi-hats. Listen: the hats breathe.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-pat="{&quot;bpm&quot;:92,&quot;swing&quot;:54,&quot;rows&quot;:{&quot;kick&quot;:&quot;x......x..x.....&quot;,&quot;snare&quot;:&quot;....x.......x...&quot;,&quot;chh&quot;:&quot;t.h.t.h.t.h.t.h.&quot;}}"><p><b>Swing 54 %.</b> A little swing. Listen: it loosens.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-pat="{&quot;bpm&quot;:92,&quot;swing&quot;:62,&quot;rows&quot;:{&quot;kick&quot;:&quot;x......x..x.....&quot;,&quot;snare&quot;:&quot;....x.......x...&quot;,&quot;chh&quot;:&quot;t.h.t.h.t.h.t.h.&quot;}}"><p><b>Swing 62 %.</b> More swing, the manual's other suggestion. Listen: a hip-hop bounce.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-pat="{&quot;bpm&quot;:92,&quot;swing&quot;:62,&quot;quant&quot;:&quot;OFF&quot;,&quot;rows&quot;:{&quot;kick&quot;:[{&quot;v&quot;:1},0,0,0,0,0,0,{&quot;v&quot;:0.7,&quot;o&quot;:5},0,0,{&quot;v&quot;:0.9,&quot;o&quot;:-3},0,0,0,0,0],&quot;snare&quot;:[0,0,0,0,{&quot;v&quot;:0.95,&quot;o&quot;:7},0,0,0,0,0,0,0,{&quot;v&quot;:1,&quot;o&quot;:9},0,0,{&quot;v&quot;:0.45,&quot;o&quot;:4}],&quot;chh&quot;:&quot;t.h.t.h.t.h.t.h.&quot;}}"><p><b>Timing correct OFF.</b> The snare and some kicks are played a little late, by hand. Listen: lazy and loose. J Dilla is known for turning quantize off (Wikipedia).</p></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Akai MPC":

- DJ Shadow, *Endtroducing* (1996), made on an MPC60 MKII
- J Dilla, known for turning off the quantize
- Kanye West, much of *The College Dropout* (2004), on an MPC (model not named)

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>A sampler plays…</b></p><ul><li>Sounds you recorded into it</li><li>Only built-in circuits</li><li>Only piano</li><li>Nothing</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 15.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Swing 50 % means…</b></p><ul><li>Straight, no swing</li><li>A full triplet</li><li>Half speed</li><li>Half volume</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 44.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Timing correct OFF keeps…</b></p><ul><li>Notes where you played them</li><li>Every note on the grid</li><li>Only the kick</li><li>The tempo at 50</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 43.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="2"><p><b>How many pads does it have?</b></p><ul><li>4</li><li>8</li><li>16</li><li>88</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 18.</p></div>
```

**For teachers**

Linn, Roger, and David Battino. *MPC60 Software Version 3.1 Operator's Manual*. Roger Linn Design, 2002, [www.polynominal.com/akai-mpc60/akai-mpc60-manual.pdf](https://www.polynominal.com/akai-mpc60/akai-mpc60-manual.pdf). 12-bit samples at 40 kHz (p. 15), 16 Levels (pp. 21-22), 96 ppq (p. 26), timing correct and swing 50-75 % (pp. 43-44), specifications (p. 218). No panel drawing: the faithful MPC60 panel takes its parts from pp. 11-13, 18, 21-22, positions guessed.
